description:
Universal Missile Regeneration
Version 1.0.0 for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Author: kemptastic

What is Universal Missile Regeneration?
Inspired by Missiles & Sundry by DatonKallandor.

Universal Missile Regeneration (UMR) gives eligible finite-ammo missile launchers combat-time ammunition regeneration while preserving their normal firing behavior.

The goal is to make missiles remain useful throughout longer/larger fights without redesigning the weapons themselves.

By default, UMR works for eligible vanilla and modded missile launchers, and it applies the same core regeneration rules to player and NPC ships.

No third-party mod dependency is required.

LunaLib is optional but recommended. Some settings can only be changed with LunaLib installed.

Note! - Missile regeneration is not currently reflected in tooltips.
This is not a table or direct weapon edit, this is a dynamically applying script that runs primarily during combat. This may be a feature in future versions though.

Main Features

Regenerates ammunition for eligible finite-ammo missile launchers.
Works for most modded missile weapons automatically, without requiring a permanent per-mod integration.
Preserves a launcher's burst/salvo size by refilling in burst-sized packets.
Firing more missiles during an active refill timer does not reset the reload progress.
Expanded Missile Racks and compatible ammo-capacity bonuses can be refilled up to the increased live ammo cap.
Extra ammo capacity does not make the refill interval faster.
Weapons that already have native ammo regeneration are not affected.
UMR prevents UMR-managed launchers from double-dipping with vanilla Missile Autoloader.
Includes player-local blacklist and timing/packet override CSVs.
Includes lower-authority third-party compatibility CSVs for mod-author integration.
Includes dedicated OFF / SUMMARY / VERBOSE / TRACE logging, with it's own seperate log file generated in the same folder as starsector.log.
Does not require a new campaign. Should be safe to remove at any time.
Version Checker enabled.

How UMR Works

Spoiler
Regeneration Quantity
Spoiler
UMR does not simply return one missile at a time to every launcher.

By default, its refill packet is the weapon's authored base burst size.

Examples:

Single-shot launcher: Refills 1 missile at a time.
2-shot burst launcher: Refills 2 at a time.
4-shot burst launcher: Refills 4 at a time.
etc

This means a burst launcher gets a usable salvo back instead of slowly receiving individual missiles that may not match its authored firing pattern.

A new refill timer does not begin until at least one complete refill packet is missing.

Once a refill chain is running:

firing again does not reset the timer;
external ammo additions do not erase earned progress;
UMR re-reads the weapon's live ammo and max ammo when the refill completes;
the final cap/remainder refill can be smaller than the normal packet when necessary.

Example for a 50-ammo launcher with a 4-ammo refill packet:

... 40 -> 44 -> 48 -> 50

That final reload will only be +2 missiles to not go over capacity.

Regeneration Timing
Spoiler
Each burst/clip of missiles is regenerated according to a custom ruleset.

First a full magazine reload time is set. This is how long it takes to regenerate the full magazine before any modifiers affect the ammo capacity. Missiles are then reloaded in increments determined by the burst size.
Small Mount = 90 seconds
Medium Mount = 115 seconds
Large Mount = 135 seconds

So for example a Harpoon MRM is a small mount that has a base magazine of 3 missiles and burst size of 1. So we regenerate 1 missile every 30 seconds. (90/3)

If a missile weapon only has a capacity of 1, we subtract 20 seconds from that timer. (S:70, M:95, L:115)
So a reaper torpedo (small mount) will regenerate 1 missile every 70 seconds.

If a missile weapon fires in bursts it will wait till a full burst is ready to regenerate.
For example, the Hammer Barrage is a large mount with a base magazine of 20 missiles and a burst of 4.
135/20 = 6.75 seconds per missile, times burst size of 4, which becomes 27 seconds. So a Hammer Barrage will regen 4 missiles at a time, once every 27 seconds.

UMR also has a safety floor of 1.4x the weapons refire delay to make sure we never regen missiles faster than the weapon itself reloads. If the regen time based off magazine size would be faster than the safety floor, we  use the safety floor as our regen time. The regen interval cannot become shorter than this number.

For example, the Swarmer SRM is a small mount with an 80 size magazine.
- Refire delay is 5.6 seconds so our safety floor becomes 7.84 seconds (5.6 x 1.4 = 7.84)
- 90 seconds divided by 80 missiles means 1.125 seconds per missile.
- Burst size of 4 would mean 4 missiles regen every 4.5 seconds, however this is faster than the refire delay of 5.6 seconds and our safety floor of 7.84 seconds.
- So to prevent turning it into an infinite fire weapon and negating ammo entirely, we use the safety floor instead, so the Swarmer actually reloads a burst of 4 missiles every 7.84 seconds.

This prevents very fast-firing burst launchers from regenerating full packets at an excessively aggressive rate simply because of magazine math.

Any modifiers to total ammo capacity, like Expanded Missile Racks do not affect regen speed in any way.

You can modify safety floor and all timings in settings.json.
"umrBaseFullMagTargetSeconds": 90.0,  ::: Base value for full mag regen in seconds
"umrSingleAmmoReductionSeconds": 20.0, ::: Subtract this many seconds for single ammo weapons
"umrMediumAdditionSeconds": 25.0, ::: Seconds added to full mag regen for Medium mount weapons. (90+25=115)
"umrLargeAdditionSeconds": 45.0, ::: Seconds added to full mag regen for Large mount weapons. (90+45=135)
"umrSafetyFloorEnabled": true, ::: Set to false to disable safety floor
"umrSafetyMultiplier": 1.4, ::: Safety floor multiplier

Modded Missile Support
Spoiler
Eligible third-party missile support is enabled by default. You can also disable this in settings.json.
"umrThirdPartyGameplayEnabled": true

If you want UMR active only for eligible vanilla missiles:

"umrThirdPartyGameplayEnabled": false

UMR uses the same general classifier for vanilla and source-attributed modded missile weapons.

This means many ordinary finite-ammo modded launchers can work automatically.

That said, some heavily scripted/resource-based weapons may not behave like ordinary finite-ammo launchers.

For those cases UMR includes:

local blacklist support;
local timing/packet overrides;
third-party compatibility blacklist/override files;
detailed logging for investigation.

Missile Autoloader Compatibility
Spoiler
UMR-managed weapons are prevented from simultaneously receiving normal vanilla Missile Autoloader refills.

This avoids double-dipping.

UMR does not globally delete Missile Autoloader or globally alter every missile WeaponSpec.

Unmanaged/blacklisted weapons can still retain normal vanilla Autoloader behavior where applicable.

By default, UMR also provides two convenience policies in the LunaLib settings menu:

Hide Missile Autoloader - hides it from the ordinary player Add Hullmod picker.*
Suppress NPC Random Missile Autoloader - conservatively removes provably random generated NPC copies when they would be wasted.

*If Autoloader is already equipped when the mod is enabled, you can still see the hullmod equipped to your ship and in the hullmod picking menu, so you can still easily unequip it.

Both are Enabled by default

Already-installed, built-in, permanent, S-modded, authored, and ambiguous copies are preserved under the relevant rules.

Without LunaLib, UMR still works normally and both shipped defaults remain enabled.

Configuring UMR

Spoiler
Additional Settings.json Values
Spoiler
umrLoggingLevel = (OFF/SUMMARY/VERBOSE/TRACE)
- Currently summary by default. Can be turned off to prevent logging or set to higher detail level for better debugging support & data collection. Trace is highest level.

umrEnableNonMissileLimitedAmmo = (true/false)
- Currently nonfunctional. Planned to enable regen for other non-missile limited ammo weapons in a future version.

umrPerformanceTelemetryEnabled = (true/false)
- Measures UMR’s own combat processing time and frame-budget usage for diagnostics.

umrAiTelemetryEnabled = (true/false)
- Collects read-only statistics on whether/how quickly normal AI ships use regenerated ammunition. It does not alter AI behavior.

Blacklist.csv
Spoiler
Found in mod folder: data\config\umr\weapon_blacklist.csv

You can add weapon IDs to this file to exclude them from UMR.
Useful if a weapon really should never have any ammo regenerated, like if a mod adds some kind of one shot nuke missile for example.
Also useful as temporary measure if a weapon happens to be crashing the game when UMR affects it/gives it regen.

Columns:
weapon_id = exact weapon ID

reason & source_or_comment
- These are just fields for writing human readable notes for yourself.

NOTE! If a weapon ID is not present in the game, nothing bad should happen, so if you add a modded weapon ID to the blacklist, then disable that mod, you should not need to remove it from the blacklist. Everything should load up and continue on without issue.

Overrides.csv
Spoiler
Found in mod folder: data\config\umr\weapon_overrides.csv

weapon_id = Exact weapon ID
burst_or_packet_size_override = #
full_mag_target_seconds_override = #
packet_regen_seconds_override = #
safety_multiplier_override = #
disable_safety_floor = true/false
*if blank, then no per-weapon disable instruction
reason = human readable notes
source_or_comment = human readable notes

These lets you change, per weapon:
refill packet size;
full-mag target;
direct packet interval;
safety multiplier;
whether the safety floor is disabled.

See above sections for more details on what these values do.
As with the Blacklist, you do not need to delete an entry if it is no longer present in your game. If UMR does not find a weapon ID it will just ignore the entry.

Third-party integration
Spoiler
in "\data\config\umr" you will find two additional csv files "third_party_blacklist.csv" and "third_party_overrides.csv"

These provide the same blacklist/override concepts as the local files, but use integration-specific schemas containing row_id and source_mod_id. Other mods or compatibility packs can contribute rows at these same merged paths, and UMR will load them automatically.

As with the base CSVs, if for whatever reason UMR does not find a matching weapon ID it will just ignore the entry.

Configuration Precedence
Spoiler
How CSVs are priotised highest to lowest:

1. hard/native/system/helper exclusion
2. local user blacklist
3. local user override
4. third-party blacklist
5. third-party override
6. global settings
7. defaults

So local player configuration always outranks third-party contribution rows.

See the full README for examples and complete field descriptions:
UMR README

Logging and Bug Reports

Spoiler
UMR writes its own dedicated log:

UniversalMissileRegeneration.log

Logging levels:

OFF
No routine UMR diagnostic logging.

SUMMARY - Default
Recommended for normal play. Includes bounded startup/config/registry/battle summaries and meaningful warnings/errors.

VERBOSE
Recommended for weapon-specific compatibility reports and large-mod-set data contributions. Adds candidate/refill/provenance/configuration details.

TRACE
Deep timing/state diagnostics. Much higher log volume; intended for targeted investigation.

UMR also has separate read-only performance and AI telemetry switches, both OFF by default.

They do not change regeneration rules or AI behavior.

Help UMR with Large Mod Sets

Spoiler
If you use a large mod list, your normal gameplay can help identify unusual launchers that may need compatibility handling.

For detailed field data:

"umrLoggingLevel": "VERBOSE"

Then play normal campaign or simulation battles and submit:

UMR version;
Starsector version;
relevant mod list / mod versions;
UniversalMissileRegeneration.log;
starsector.log;
affected weapon/mod if you noticed a specific issue;
whether you are reporting a visible bug or simply contributing telemetry.

GitHub Issues:
UMR Issues

Save Compatibility

Spoiler
UMR does not require a new campaign and should be safe to remove at any time.

Release testing covered:

existing saves;
save/reload;
new games;
clean Starsector + UMR;
large modded environments;
removal from a disposable save copy.

The disposable campaign loaded and saved again successfully with UMR disabled.

As with any Starsector mod-list change, back up important saves first.

Performance Impact

Spoiler
UMR was profiled during normal modded gameplay before release, including large fleet battles.

Across 7 completed battles and 46,922 combat frames, UMR averaged:

Average UMR processing time: 47.026 microseconds per frame
Average share of a 60 FPS frame budget: 0.282%

For reference, a game running at 60 FPS has about 16.67 milliseconds available for each frame. UMR was using about 0.047 milliseconds of that on average in the measured battles.

The heaviest completed battle in the profiling set averaged approximately:

0.413% of a 60 FPS frame budget

So even the heaviest measured engagement remained well below 1% average frame-time usage by UMR.

These tests were performed in a heavily modded environment rather than a minimal test setup, and included normal regeneration, weapon classification, Missile Autoloader compatibility handling, and SUMMARY-level diagnostics.

A few caveats:

These are measured results from the test system and mod environment, not a guarantee for every computer or mod list.
Larger battles naturally create more managed weapon instances.
VERBOSE and especially TRACE logging intentionally perform substantially more diagnostic logging than the normal SUMMARY default.
The optional performance and AI telemetry systems are disabled by default in the public release.

License & Disclaimers

Spoiler
UMR is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0.

Required Notice: Copyright 2026 kemptastic. Universal Missile Regeneration.

Full license:
LICENSE

Custom made AI tools were used to assist in the development, documentation, creating testing scripts and other limited aspects of this mod. An extensive amount of man hours were put in by myself to among other things, ensure stability of code, accuracy of any AI contribution, and all actual testing.

Feedback Welcome

Spoiler
This is UMR's first public release, so feedback is super helpful.

In particular, I would appreciate:

reports of unusual missile weapons that should be excluded or tuned differently;
mod-author compatibility contributions;
large-mod-set telemetry;
balance/feel feedback;
documentation improvements;
feature ideas.
